title: Model output IP & export controls — scratchpad
content:
Purpose: quick, personal checklist + talking points when counterparties start asking for broad assignment / unlimited rights over model outputs, or want to impose export-control burdens on us.

Top-level takeaways (short):
- We should avoid blanket assignment of model outputs unless the customer is paying enterprise+ and we get reciprocal IP/indemnity and a narrow scope.
- Prefer license grants to the customer with explicit carveouts for Redwood model improvements, training artifacts, and internal telemetry.
- Export-control asks: push back on any requirement that forces us to host customer data in restricted geographies unless contractually scoped and priced.

Notes to self (fragments):
- "Customer claims ownership of 'outputs' generated by the model fed with customer data" -> this is ambiguous: outputs can contain model-learned patterns. Need to define: derived vs. verbatim.
- SIG: product wants a single-sentence risk bullet for sales: "We grant you a license to use outputs for your business — Redwood retains rights to model improvements and aggregated telemetry." Keep it short.
- Engineering highlight: if customer wants export control provenance logs (per-request trace), that's operationally heavy; escalate to infra for feasibility/cost.

Clauses to flag (language to watch for):
1) "All outputs, deliverables and work product" (too broad) -> propose: "Outputs (customer-provided prompts and generated content) excluding model weights, training data, internal evaluation sets, and aggregated telemetry; subject to Redwood's retained rights below."
2) Assignment/Work-for-hire -> automatic assignment across all future outputs is a non-starter. Offer a timed license or customer ownership only of customer-supplied content + direct human-written deliverables.
3) Required export-control compliance / data localization for Redwood’s whole platform -> limit to: "for Customer's data processed under this Agreement, Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts" and then put cost and SLA implications into SOW.
4) Indemnity tied to outputs accuracy -> we usually accept limited carveouts for gross negligence, but not for hallucinations. Push for clear limitations of liability and disclaimers for model-generated factuality.

Suggested fallback redlines (quick snippets we can paste):
- "Customer License to Outputs: Subject to payment and compliance with the Agreement, Redwood hereby grants Customer a worldwide, non-exclusive, perpetual, royalty-free license to use, reproduce, and modify Outputs that are generated solely from Customer-provided prompts and Customer Content, for Customer's internal business purposes and for its end customers, provided that Redwood retains all rights in and to the underlying models, model weights, training data, and aggregated telemetry and analytics ("Redwood Retained Rights")."
- "Export & Localization: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to comply with Customer's written data localization requests for Customer Data set forth in an executed SOW. Additional costs and time required to satisfy such requests will be handled via change order."
- "No Assignment of Model IP: No provision in this Agreement shall be construed to transfer title or ownership in the Redwood models, model weights, or any model enhancements developed or derived by Redwood, even if Customer provides prompts or datasets."

Risk scoring (quick):
- Broad assignment of outputs: HIGH (exposure to downstream IP claims + model improvement leakage)
- Required on-prem/offshore-only hosting: MEDIUM-HIGH (operational cost + delays)
- Unlimited export-control warranties: HIGH (legal complexity, penalties)
- Per-request provenance and logs retention: MEDIUM (cost + privacy)

Deal-specific negotiation playbook (one-liners for sales call):
- If they want "all outputs" ownership: "We can grant usage rights for all outputs; ownership of our models and improvements has to remain with Redwood — if you need further exclusivity, we can discuss an enterprise arrangement with financial commitment."
- If they push localization: "We’ve run localization for similar customers; it’s feasible but we’ll need to scope throughput, backups, and an implementation timeline. Let's capture that in a SOW and costs."
- If they demand accuracy warranties: "We provide commercially reasonable efforts and will commit to uptime/service levels, but model outputs are 'as-is' regarding factual accuracy; we can negotiate limited remedies for material regressions tied to a defined eval set."

Open questions / follow-ups (to triage):
- Can infra produce per-request provenance logs at 1-year retention without massive cost? /cc @Diego Ramos
- Pricing play: what is the uplift for localization + signed indemnities? Need pricing input from finance.
- Is there precedent where we granted exclusive output rights? Who signed and what did we get in return? Ask sales ops for a redline exemplar.

Technical notes for engineering handoff:
- If customer wants to exclude outputs from being used in offline model evals / aggregated telemetry, we need a flag at ingest time or a tenant-level opt-out. That impacts cache/tokens and eval sampling.
- Consider adding a "do-not-learn" tag for customer prompts; this creates complexity for batching and cache hits — surface to serving runtime team (ticket: MLF-privacy-88).

Handy references (internal):
- Confluence: Model Output Policy (link above)
- Legal precedent: contract X-789 (customer requested assignment; we accepted license + $350k uplift) -> pull redline from legal repo.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Draft counterlanguage for assignment/outputs and circulate to Priya + Diego (due EOD)
- [ ] Confirm infra costs for logs + retention (Diego)
- [ ] Get pricing uplift table from Finance for localization and exclusivity (Priya)
- [ ] Save exemplar redlines from Sales Ops (Ava)

Random notes / scratch:
- If they insist on assignment because they believe outputs will be monetized: propose a revenue-share clause for derivatives instead of outright assignment.
- Watch for 'source code' or "derivative works" language — often used to expand claim scope.
- Keep the sales-facing line short and simple: license for outputs; Redwood keeps models/weights/telemetry.

End of scratchpad.

(Comments-to-self: do not escalate to 'final' language without infra cost estimates; keep this doc as the working stash for next negotiation.)
